steps.beforeInstructorMessage: You’ve bricked the flop but still hold two overcards, and villain tosses out a tiny "why not" bet into a big pot.
steps.question: Facing a tiny stab into a large pot with two overcards and no made hand, do you peel, raise, or simply fold the air?

gradingSpecJson.responseIncorrect: There is a better line in this node.
gradingSpecJson.followUpContent: With two overcards and no pair, your raw equity might hover around the high twenties against a typical flop betting range—nothing special on its own. But when that bet is a true min-click into a pot of several thousand chips, you may only need around 4% equity to justify calling once, which turns almost any hand with overcards into a profitable peel. The mistake is treating all bets as equal: calling a pot-sized barrel with the same hand is a disaster, while calling a token flop stab is simply buying a very cheap shot at top pair or a strong turn card. Strong players constantly compare bet size to pot size and adjust; they defend wider versus tiny bets and tighten up as the price goes up. Here, the microscopic flop bet means calling with overcards is a clear, disciplined way to realize your equity.
